sub_scenario.one_line: release operations lead: ask for a recovery accommodation before confirming

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the handover board and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The on-call calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Routine afternoon release notes do not tire me. Case-note 1.
Notes are different from recovery work. Case-note 2.
They do not follow an overnight page. Case-note 3.
Someone new shadowed me in the release room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the pager rotations into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After Tuesday's overnight pager rotation, I closed the handover board at 10:45 and slept until noon. Case-note 7.
The rotation consumed the morning. Case-note 8.
I did not have a usable afternoon reserve. Case-note 9.
I can join a short social lunch after daytime duty. Case-note 4.
So ordinary team time is manageable. Case-note 5.
Yes, when I have slept normally. Case-note 6.
I archived last cycle's notes on the on-call calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The new pager tone has interrupted my sleep for three weeks. Case-note 10.
The disruption is ongoing. Case-note 11.
Quiet nights have not fixed it. Case-note 12.
A vendor call about the handover board ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the release room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the pager rotations.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the on-call calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
My physiotherapy for the shoulder is booked Thursday at 17:30 and the clinic cannot shift it. Case-note 13.
That is a fixed same-day booking. Case-note 14.
Missing it restarts the treatment sequence. Case-note 15.
I sketched next week's plan for the pager rotations before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the handover board updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Palpitations mean I avoid late coffee when a shift has already broken sleep. Case-note 16.
So caffeine cannot extend the day. Case-note 17.
I plan less rather than push through. Case-note 18.
I compared two options for the on-call calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the release room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The team email expects confirmation for Thursday afternoon's offsite. What response fits my week?
